Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CTET Paper 2 asks on Data Handling

Questions cover organising data with tally marks and frequency tables, reading and drawing pictographs and bar graphs, and calculating the average (arithmetic mean).

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • Tally marks are grouped in fives — the fifth crosses the previous four.
  • A pictograph uses a symbol for a fixed number of items and always needs a key/scale.
  • In a bar graph the bars have equal width and the height is proportional to the value.
  • Mean = (sum of all observations) ÷ (number of observations).
  • The mean always lies between the smallest and largest values.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ignoring the key/scale of a pictograph.
  • Drawing bars of unequal width in a bar graph.
  • Dividing by the wrong count when finding the mean.

quiz.title: CTET Data Handling Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The mean of the first five prime numbers is:
questions.explanation: The first five prime numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7, and 11. Their sum = 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 11 = 28. The mean = 28 / 5 = 5.6.

questions.q: The range of the data set: 17, 32, 41, 19, 25, 48, 12, 29 is:
questions.explanation: Range is the difference between the highest and lowest observations in the data. Highest value = 48, Lowest value = 12. Range = 48 - 12 = 36.

questions.q: The mean of 10 observations is 15. If 2 is added to each observation, the new mean will be:
questions.explanation: When a constant value is added to each observation of a data set, the mean increases by that same constant value. New mean = Old mean + 2 = 15 + 2 = 17.

questions.q: A coin is tossed 3rd time after getting heads twice. What is the theoretical probability of getting a tail on the 3rd toss?
questions.explanation: Coin tosses are independent events. The previous outcomes do not affect the outcome of subsequent tosses. The probability of getting a tail on any fair coin toss is always 1/2.

questions.q: In a frequency distribution, tally marks are usually bundled in groups of:
questions.explanation: Tally marks are recorded in groups of five, with the fifth line crossing diagonally through the first four, making counting easier in blocks of five.

questions.q: The mode of the data set: 4, 5, 6, 4, 3, 2, 4, 5, 6, 4, 5 is:
questions.explanation: Mode is the observation that occurs most frequently. Counting frequencies: 4 appears 4 times, 5 appears 3 times, 6 appears 2 times, 3 appears 1 time, 2 appears 1 time. Since 4 has the highest frequency (4), the mode is 4.

questions.q: When students mistakenly add all the values and divide by the total number of items when asked to find the 'median', it indicates:
options: Inability to read numbers in ascending order.
Lack of computational skills in addition.
A conceptual confusion between mean and median.
An error in understanding bar graphs.
questions.explanation: Confusing the procedure for calculating the arithmetic mean with finding the middle value (median) represents a typical conceptual misunderstanding between measures of central tendency.

questions.q: In a pie chart, a central angle of 72 degrees represents a particular category. What percentage of the total data does this category constitute?
The median of a set of 9 distinct observations is 20. If each of the largest 4 observations of the set is increased by 3, the median of the new set will:
questions.explanation: For 9 observations, the median is the 5th observation. Increasing the largest 4 observations (the 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th values) does not alter the value or position of the 5th observation. Hence, the median remains unchanged.

questions.q: A box contains 3 blue, 2 white, and 4 red marbles. If a marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is white?
questions.explanation: Total number of marbles = 3 + 2 + 4 = 9. Number of white marbles = 2. Probability = Number of favorable outcomes / Total outcomes = 2 / 9.

faq.q: How do you find the average of a data set?
faq.a: Add up all the observations and divide by how many there are. The result always lies between the least and greatest values.

faq.q: Why does a pictograph need a key?
faq.a: Because one symbol can represent many items; without the key you cannot know how many each symbol stands for.
